resolved_prompt: Compose one continuous single-view vertical image built around exactly one clearly adult woman as the only figure. Every visible face, body, and hand belongs to this same woman. Place a clearly visible strip of background above her entire hairstyle, and keep her complete crown, face, and both eyes clearly readable. The second lighting direction has authority over every actual source shape, direction, and illumination color. Keep the face and requested visible eyes readable, and make each source named by that direction visibly distinct. Give its named reflected light or fill a separate readable role. Carry the first style only through set shape, material color, surface, atmosphere, and edge treatment. Use a photorealistic adult editorial material treatment with layered border motifs and repeated decorative shapes around the subject; muted slate, clay, sage, limestone, and small pale pigment accents; powdery matte grain with absorbed material highlights; deep evening pigment values, narrow graphic paths, and tense still space; and short silhouette sections merging into the backdrop while focal edges stay firm. Treat these as material, set, pigment, and graphic properties; the second lighting direction alone supplies every actual source and illumination color. Combine it coherently with this second visual direction: Light an adult subject with an overhead skylight-like source that opens the face and shoulders, traveling across the scene to create a gradual light-to-shadow progression. The image uses enveloping diffuse light with open shadows and gentle local contrast and a warm key balanced by cool fill with natural separation across the face. Resolve both directions on the same adult subject. Give every named visual cue an obvious, concrete location on the face, clothing, silhouette, lighting, or environment. Preserve the selected medium and keep the face, eyes, visible hands, joints, garment construction, and spatial relationships coherent. Finish the single scene cleanly with text-free, logo-free, watermark-free imagery. The second lighting direction is the final illumination blueprint: all visible illumination comes only from its named sources, colors, and geometry. Its named reflected light or fill remains visibly separate from the key. The first style contributes shape, material palette, surface, atmosphere, and edge treatment. Final camera lock—let the upper body fill most of the canvas from the complete crown to a lower edge crossing the garment immediately below the waist, with both described hand gestures inside while the thighs and feet continue beyond the canvas.
